# Building Chicago Kids’ Financial Confidence: Old National Bank and The DAISIE Foundation


Share:


- Copied!


-
-
-


Only 15% of adults report learning about money primarily in school, while less than 50% report they primarily learned about money and financial concepts from their family.1


Looking to raise those numbers is a partnership between Old National Bank and the Chicago-based DAISIE Foundation, delivering initiatives that build pathways toward financial stability, personal growth, and long-term success.


In Chicago, the sixth-grade class at Howe School of Excellence received an early start on building their financial futures through a six-week financial education program, becoming the first Chicago Public Schools class to complete the initiative.


“At first I was nervous, and now I feel okay,” sixth grader Lanailah told Fox 32 Chicago. “I learned how to save my money on things that I need ... how to save money and how to invest in it.”


### Middle school financial literacy


Throughout the six-week program, Old National team members joined students in the classroom to explore important financial concepts including budgeting, saving, investing, credit and the difference between needs and wants. Students earned “DAISIE Bucks,” a classroom currency designed to reward participation and achievement.


“One of the commitments that we make … is creating opportunities of exposure. Because we know that exposure is the greatest pathway to success,” said Julie Hightower, executive board president of The DAISIE Foundation.


### Real-Life Finance® for kids


For the Howe students, the opportunities extend beyond the six-week course. Old National is also providing the Howe School of Excellence with free, lifetime access to more than 40[Real-Life Finance® education lessons](https://www.oldnational.com/about-us/community/financial-education-courses/real-life-finance/) , expanding the opportunity for students and families to continue building their financial knowledge.


The Chicago program also builds upon financial education partnerships between Old National, the DAISIE Foundation and The DAISIE Project in Milwaukee. This past May, sixth graders at Alexander Mitchell Elementary in Milwaukee completed a similar six-week program covering budgeting, saving, credit, entrepreneurship and risk management.


“At Old National, we know that strong financial habits often begin at a young age,” says Ben Joergens, Director of Financial Empowerment. “Through school partnerships, youth programming, and Family Money Talks resources, we provide age-appropriate financial education for students and families, helping build a foundation for long term financial success.”


For more information on Old National’s financial education programs and courses,[click here](https://www.oldnational.com/about-us/community/financial-education-courses/real-life-finance/) .
